newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi stake to be floated in Tel Aviv.
newsitem.headline: Leumi stake to be floated in Tel Aviv.

text.p: The Israeli government company charged with selling the state's bank shares has told Bank Leumi to prepare a prospectus for the sale of a 10 percent stake in Tel Aviv, the bank said on Wednesday.
"I estimate the prospectus will be published in May," a bank spokeswoman said.
The director of MI Holdings, the state company selling the bank shares, was not immediately available for comment.
Based on the bank's current market valuation, the offering will be for about 720 million shekels.

The directive to Leumi apparently marks a change in plans for the government. In December, MI Holdings said it was weighing a plan to float 10 percent of the bank in the United States and Europe rather than in Tel Aviv. MI Holdings is also planning to make a secondary domestic offering in Israel Discount Bank next month.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper quoted MI Holdings managing director Meir Jacobson as saying the Tel Aviv offering was unrelated to discussions on launching a new tender for a controlling interest in Bank Leumi.
Yediot Ahronoth said Edmond Safra, whose family owns the Republic National Bank of New York, was considering renewing his bid to buy a controlling share in Bank Leumi.

In 1995, Safra was the sole bidder for Leumi, Israel's second-biggest bank, but pulled out. Analysts said the family objected to Bank of Israel demands that it relinquish control of the First International Bank of Israel as a condition for acquiring Bank Leumi.
